newsitem.title: INDIA: India says foreign debt service ratio to fall.
newsitem.headline: India says foreign debt service ratio to fall.

text.p: India's external debt service ratio is expected to fall in 1996/97 (April-March) and continue declining in the future, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram has said.

In a written reply, released on Friday, to a question in parliament, Chidambaram said the ratio, defined as the ratio of debt service to current receipts, is expected to fall to about 25 percent in 1996/97 from 25.7 in the previous fiscal year.
"The debt service ratio has followed a declining trend in the recent years," the finance minister said, noting that it reached a high of 35.3 percent in 1990/91.
"The declining trend is expected to continue in future," he said.

In reply to a separate question, Chidambaram said the nation's outstanding foreign debt stood at $92.199 billion on March 31, 1996, compared to $99.008 billion one year earlier and $92.695 billion at the end of March 1994.

Last September, Chidambaram said outstanding foreign debt fell to $92.6 billion in March 1996, $6.4 billion below the peak of $99 billion in March 1995 and the lowest since 1993. The finance minister has said India should eventually trim the debt service ratio to 20 percent.
In his reply to parliament, Chidambaram said principal payments rose to $8.063 billion in 1995/96 from $6.825 billion in 1994/95 and $4.783 billion in 1993/94.
Interest payments also rose, increasing to $4.315 billion in 1995/96 from $4.099 billion in 1994/95 and $3.818 billion in 1993/94.
Total debt servicing amounted to $12.378 billion in 1995/96, up from $10.924 billion in 1994/95 and $8.601 billion in 1993/94.

"The main features of debt-management strategy followed by the government includes sustaining a high rate of growth of exports, encouraging non-debt creating capital inflows and keeping the maturity structure as well as the total amount of commercial debt under control," Chidambaram said.
The strategy helped the nation to lower the ratio of debt to gross domestic product (GDP) to 28.71 percent in 1995/96 from 41 percent in 1991/92, he added.
